recipes.name: Dutch Apple Pie with Oatmeal Streusel
ingredients_raw: 5 cups apples - peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Make the apple pie: Place apple slices in a large bowl. Mix white sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and allspice together in a separate bowl until combined; sprinkle over apples and toss until evenly coated.
Remove pie shell from freezer; pour apple mixture into pie shell and dot with butter. Lay a sheet of aluminum foil lightly on top of filling, but do not seal.
Bake pie in the preheated oven for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, make the streusel topping: Mix flour, oats, brown sugar, lemon zest, and cinnamon in a medium bowl until combined. Cut in butter until mixture is crumbly. Remove pie from oven and sprinkle streusel on top.

Reduce heat to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Return pie to oven and bake until streusel is browned and apples are tender, 30 to 35 minutes more. Cover loosely with aluminum foil to prevent excess browning.

raw_recipe.headline: Dutch Apple Pie with Oatmeal Streusel
raw_recipe.description: The crunchy streusel topping on this apple pie adds an extra dimension of flavor and texture. Serve warm with vanilla ice cream for a winning dessert!

review.reviewBody: This is an excellent recipe. A couple little hints may help those that are having problems. I didn't freeze my pie crust. I lightly brushed the crust with a beaten egg white, let it dry (while I was peeling apples) then put it in the oven at 400 degrees for 5 minutes. Also, adding a heaping TLB of INSTANT TAPIOCA to the apples when you toss them will thicken any excess juice without adding additional flour. It won't change the taste. I do this to all my fruit pies whether the recipe calls for it or not.

Wow, wow, WOW! Fantastic pie! I'm extremely fussy about apple pie and this is the best one I've ever made in thirty years! I did tweak the recipe slightly, taking into consideration all of the previous comments. Here's what I did: 

1. Used a good homemade all butter crust and a glass pie plate 2. Used half Fuji and half Granny Smith apples, totalling 3 pounds (a little more than five cups) 3. Increased the flour to a rounded quarter cup 4. Omitted the lemon zest (don't like lemon and apple together) and the allspice (didn't have any) and substitued quick oats for rolled ones.

I also discovered that you can do the initial baking of the apples and crust ahead of time. I had to leave, so I just took it out of the oven, lightly covered with foil and when I returned 3 hours later to finish baking it, it worked out great. 

With the full three pounds of apples I used, and all that streusel topping, it looks HUGE before it bakes but it comes out the perfect size.

With a glass pie plate I dropped the oven temp to 360 degrees and I ended up baking it much longer (at least ten or fifteen minutes longer) until I could view the browned crust on the bottom (easy with a glass pan) This is crucial because otherwise you get a soggy crust on the bottom.

We ate the pie after it had totally cooled and the slices held together perfectly. Delicious! Give it a try!

Love ❤ this versatile pie/cobbler recipe! Started making it in 2005 to use up boxes of apples donated to a church homeless shelter in Seattle. To avoid extra fuss, skip the bottom crust and bake in deep dish pans doubling or tripling the recipe as needed. To enhance distinct flavors of apple varieties, use only half the sugars. I like the toasted oat flavor and have never used foil, however if your oven runs hot or has a fan you may need to. Alternative ingredients: Spice: pumpkin, cardamon or nutmeg Nuts: walnuts, almonds or pecans Zest: lemon or orange Fruit: peaches or plums, strawberry-rhubarb. For softer fruits use "quick oats".

I loved it. I pre baked the pastry until it was brown before filling. I always do this and find the crust doesn't get soggy. My family wanted more apple so I will increase the Apple by 1 cup next time. I found the recipe didn't require any other thickener but the flour. I was careful to mix the apples and flour until they were completely combined before adding to the crust.. I think how much apple or thickener needed depends on how much the apple you're using cooks down while baking. This pie was a cross between a pie and a crisp. I found I had to explain this to my family.

This is so good. I decided to make it because I love apple pie and apple crisp and this is like a combo of both. I used a mix of fuji and granny smith apples. After reading other's reviews, I used 3 tbsps flour in apple mixture. I also brushed crust with egg white before adding apples. I didn't put crust in freezer and I used a store bought crust. Absolutely the best. Will make many times over. Oh and I also let it rest an hour before slicing just to help it settle a bit and not have liquids run.

I have made this a couple of times now. It is exactly what I was looking for. I have an apple tree, an old fashioned heirloom tree called Early Strawberry. They are wonderful for applesauce but usually cook up too quickly to make a good pie (they make almost an applesauce pie when cooked the recommended time). So I bake this crust beforehand, put my apples in, and top with the streusel. I only cook long enough to brown the streusel and it's perfect! They are a marvelous, tart apple. So good!

Amazing apple pie!!! I did the egg wash on the frozen crust and it helped. I also used 3 kind of apples - honey crisp, Granny Smith, and a fuji. Everyone loved the pie and said it was the best pie. I was told I will be bringing this to every family gathering from now on.

Very good pie. I made some changes. I added an additional 1/3 C of brown sugar and 3/4 tsp salt to the sugar/spice mix.
I added 1/4 C ground walnuts to the topping.
I lengthened initial baking time to 15 mins.
Simple and delicious. I'll be using this pie and topping recipe going forward.

Made this for my family - Christmas Eve dinner. It received 5 stars from everyone! I took the advice for the crust and brushed with a beaten egg white and baked it for 7 minutes @ 375. I also cooked the Granny Smith apples (used about 10 or 11 medium sized & sliced thin) in a heavy iron skillet for 5 minutes then added the sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg mixture but used 2 tbsp tapioca instead of flour and cooked another 10 minutes. Added Apple filling, baked for 10 minutes, then put the streusel topping on and baked for 25 min. with foil placed on top. I allowed the pie to cool for several hours to allow juices to set before cutting. Served w/ vanilla ice cream.

This is one awesome pie! 
Yes, I tweaked it a bit after reading a bunch of the reviews: added additional apples, additional flour, additional cinnamon, made my own pie crust, and precooked it 5 minutes before adding apples, and cooked the pie for 50 minutes, but I’m not counting that against the author of this recipe. 
I consider this to be one of the best pies I’ve ever made- it’s THAT good!
I used 2 cans of Aldi fried apples in cinnamon sauce and skipped crust, putting it in casserole dish. El perfecto
The streusel recipe made way too much streusel for the pie. I’d probably make half as much next time.
I would add a little salt and a tablespoon white sugar

The flavor was wonderful❤️ When baking, the topping and crust as far as I could see were browned( metal pan) I even put a piece of aluminum foil over the top the last 5 minutes (30 mins)but the apples inside were somewhat more crisp than I would have liked. I did throw in a handful of fresh cranberries😋 and backed off a little on all of the sugar measurements since I don't like her super sweet pie 👍 not sure if leaving the skins on but cutting smaller pieces affected the cooking time and not sure how much longer I could have baked it without the top getting really overdone. suggestions welcome! Would definitely make it again!
I have made this recipe for a few years now. Everybody loves it

This was an amazing pie! I did double the flour and the spices and was happy that it wasn't a soupy pie. I would make this recipe again for sure. I used less sugar than called for because I was using fuji apples but would use the amount in the recipe if I was baking with Granny Smith.

I used homemade pie crust, 5 large apples, increased the spices, used less sugar than called for (⅓ cup brown sugar Splenda blend) and reduced butter to ¼ cup. I didn’t care for the streusel topping- too much flour, and too much topping for the size of the pie (9”). Next time I’ll cut back on the flour in the streusel topping and add more oats. The texture and taste of the pie was good.
